A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoMo-0D study and contain the main text and appendices A-M. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable matching of methods, equations, figures, tables, and results.

before.justification: v3 reports original FoMo-0D benchmark performance, runtime measurements, ablations, attention analyses, and synthetic and OpenOOD generalization results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds model-depth ablation results and a restricted benchmark-subset comparison.

M1.justification: The GMM prior, outlier synthesis, data reuse and transformations, router attention, training objective, and zero-shot inference procedure remain unchanged. The default four-layer model is retained; the smaller models are experimental ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 57 ADBench datasets, ten OpenOOD-derived datasets, and synthetic distribution-shift scenarios. The new 47-dataset analysis filters existing coverage without adding datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: The 26 ADBench baselines and four hyperparameter-averaged variants remain unchanged, as do the four OpenOOD comparators and three runtime comparators. The new depth ablation uses existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix F.10 introduces evaluations with one, two, and three Transformer layers alongside the default four layers, spanning 1.34-4.89 million parameters. Table 1 adds evaluation restricted to 47 datasets excluding image/text embeddings. Existing splits, preprocessing, and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.10 tests sensitivity to model depth, and Table 1 adds a check excluding embedding-derived datasets. Earlier ablations, attention case studies, and generalization analyses remain. Appendix L's proposed systematic stress tests are future work, not additional experiments.

E5.justification: The revised boxplots add 5th-95th percentile whiskers and tail points, with captions explicitly defining the mean and quartile summaries. Appendix G.3 corrects 'Wilcoxon sign test' to 'Wilcoxon signed rank test' while retaining its p-values. Existing five-seed and 1000-seed mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remains.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises all three baselines' training and inference timings; for example, kNN training changes from 1433.74 to 174157.38 ms. FoMo-0D remains at 7.7 ms per sample. Table 1 adds subset results and Table 8 adds depth-ablation results; the detailed ADBench and OpenOOD detection scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The PPD, loss, attention equations, and Appendix B definitions, lemmas, and proofs are unchanged. Section 2.1's explicit train/test disjointness statement restates the existing split setting rather than introducing a different mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims no significant performance differences from any baseline on the 47-dataset subset excluding embeddings. This adds a restricted-domain effectiveness claim. The core novelty, elimination of model selection, zero-shot inference, and headline 57-dataset claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F.10 adds an interpretation of diminishing returns from three to four layers. The Broader Impact Statement newly acknowledges that fairness and bias metrics are not considered, and Appendix L proposes controlled stress testing of generalization. Existing clean-context and static-evaluation limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract and Appendix M replace the anonymous PFN40D access link with the named FoMo-0D GitHub repository. A new runtime footnote identifies PyOD/scikit-learn BallTree implementations and possible extra kNN computations. The depth ablation also supplies parameter counts.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to TabPFN v2, TabICL, scikit-learn, and PyOD, extending the PFN discussion and supporting implementation disclosures. The central positioning as the first PFN for tabular outlier detection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title adds 'Tabular'; Section 2.1 is rewritten to distinguish clean inductive and contaminated transductive settings and revise terminology. Several explanatory paragraphs and the impact statement are edited, with publication headers added. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 now displays AUROC distributions; the earlier rank distribution is redrawn and moved to Appendix Figure 17. Table 1 gains a subset row and Table 8 presents the depth ablation. Captions, table placement, and pagination change, while the other 26 figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The depth ablation and subset analysis add useful checks, while clearer task definitions, distribution reporting, and access instructions make the evidence easier to assess. These limited gains are partly offset by the new Table 1 caption's claim of no significant differences despite several p>0.95 entries indicating superiority under the paper's stated convention.
